Subject: Mid-term top-up & renewal concessions (OptiHealth)

Aditya —

We’re ramping faster than expected and need to discuss a mid-term top-up to our Dedicated GPU pool ahead of the Feb renewal. Current commit is 60 GPUs but we’re trending to 110 effective Jan-Feb (peak batch/embedding workloads). Procurement asked for: a) a short-term top-up pricing for the remainder of this year, b) how that top-up could convert into a committed reserve at renewal (discounts/step-downs), and c) any SLA/throughput guarantees tied to commit size.

I’ve attached our updated capacity forecast (OptiHealth_MAPP_v3.xlsx). Could you share an outline of options and an initial price range? Also looping in procurement.

Thanks,

Thanks for the forecast — saw the attachment. High-level we can support a temporary top-up (reserved hourly or short-term commit) and offer a conversion path with a stepped discount if you convert to a longer commit at renewal. To scope precisely we need: 1) expected sustained baseline GPUs in Jan (not just peak), 2) percent of workload that is latency-sensitive (needs throughput SLAs), and 3) any hard blackout/maintenance windows.

I’m looping Marissa (pricing) & Karthik (capacity/throughput) to put together two options: a 3‑month top-up pilot with hourly reservation pricing, and a mid-term amendment that converts to a 12‑month committed pool with a conversion discount. Will attach an initial sketch in the next few hours.

Subject: Options: short-term top-up vs conversion to commit — pricing & SLOs

Ben / team —

We put together two pragmatic options after reviewing the MAPP forecast. Summary below; see attached offer PDF for numbers and examples.

Option A — Short-term top-up (Nov 17 — Feb 28):
- Add 50 GPUs to current pool as an hourly-reserved top-up.
- Hourly rate = $X/hr (list price) with a 10% temporary uplift discount for customers converting to commit at renewal.
- No change to existing SLA; we guarantee node availability for 99.5% of hours above baseline (measured per calendar week).

Option B — Convert to expanded commit at renewal (12‑month):
- Convert the additional 50 GPUs into a 12‑month reserved pool effective Mar 1.
- Step discount: 12% off list for first 6 months, 8% thereafter (effective blended ~10%).
- Throughput guarantee: we’ll target 95th-percentile tail latency at current seq lengths; if we miss SLO by >2 weeks, credit structure applies (details in doc).

Other notes:
- We can fast-track capacity on our Dedicated fleet to meet a Jan 1 ramp, but that requires a signed amendment + 2 weeks lead for provisioning.
- For procurement: we’ll accept a single amendment that covers the Nov top-up and a conversion clause — simpler operationally.

Attaching the initial offer. If this direction looks good, we’ll have Soojin draft the amendment summary and legal redline bullets.

Thanks,
Marissa

3) Early conversion credit — if we convert the top-up to commit before Mar 1, is the 10% uplift discount still guaranteed?

Procurement prefers a single amendment and wants to run a DocuSign for sign-off once pricing is agreed. Can you also provide a simple one‑page summary for procurement to circulate?

Thanks — looping Sanjay (CTO) to confirm the technical ramp.

See responses inline to procurement’s asks and an attachment with the amendment summary (amendment_summary_20261118.docx). Key points: 

1) 24‑month floor: we can extend the conversion path to a 24‑month commit with an improved floor discount (16% fixed) if OptiHealth signs within 30 days of the top-up start. This is a commercial concession tied to speed-to-sign.

2) SLA credits: our credit table (attached) maps missed weekly availability or throughput SLOs to $/GPU‑hour credits. Example: missing weekly availability by >1.5% → 3% credit on that week’s GPU charges; missing throughput target for >2 weeks → $0.75/GPU‑hour credit for impacted hours (escalates with duration).

3) Early conversion: yes — if conversion is executed before Mar 1, the 10% temporary uplift discount converts into the first-month conversion discount and is stackable with the 24‑month floor only if Converted within 30 days (cannot be combined with other promotional programs).

Operationally: we’ll need a signed amendment and PO. Our provisioning lead time is 10 business days after countersign. I’ve attached the amendment summary and a one‑page procurement brief.

- Ben / procurement: confirm whether you want the 12‑month or 24‑month floor option (and sign window).
